title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement:
Slide a window of `k` numbers across a list, one position at a time from left to right, and find the largest number in each window. A list of `n` numbers has `n - k + 1` windows. Try to do it in one pass over the list: looking through every window again is too slow when `k` is large.

The first line has `n` and `k`, with `k` between 1 and `n`. The second line has the `n` integers, separated by spaces. Print the largest number of each window, in order, on one line separated by spaces.

Input:

```text
8 3
1 3 -1 -3 5 3 6 7
```

Expected output:

```text
3 3 5 5 6 7
```
hints: Keep a deque of the indexes that could still be the maximum of some window, with their numbers getting smaller from front to back.
Before you add index `i` at the back, pop every index at the back whose number is no bigger than the number at `i`. It can never be a maximum again. Then the front is always the window's maximum.
Pop the front when its index has slid out of the window, which is when it's `i - k` or less.
